### Review of Deviations (1–3)

1. **`/mail` does not call the model, only lists what 07:30 sorted and reports `N newer not sorted yet`:** Sound decision. Blocking the single-threaded Telegram poll loop for up to `15 × 16 s = 4 minutes` on `/mail` would freeze the bot and time out `getUpdates`.
2. **`BRIEFING = False` constant in [mail_triage.py](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L18):** Clean, explicit, and easy to flip in a one-line commit after the shadow week.
3. **`conn.commit()` before the loop and after each `INSERT` in `mail_triage.run()`:** Necessary and well-tested (`test_run_leaves_no_open_write_while_the_model_runs`), since `llm.record_usage()` opens its own `get_db()` connection inside `ask_local()`.

---

### Findings

1. **[mail_triage.py:135](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L135) — Medium (Bug / Crash Risk): `date.fromisoformat(due)` crashes on invalid calendar dates from the local model.**
   - In `sort_one()` ([mail_triage.py:89](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L89)), `due` is validated only by regex `re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", d["due"])`. If the local model hallucinates an out-of-range calendar date matching `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` (e.g. `"2026-02-29"`, `"2026-11-31"`, `"2026-00-00"`), `sort_one()` stores it in `mail_triage.due`. Then `_line()` calls `date.fromisoformat(due)` and raises `ValueError: day is out of range for month`, crashing `/mail` and `leo.deliver()`.
   - **Fix:** Validate `due` with `date.fromisoformat(d["due"])` inside a `try...except ValueError` in `sort_one()`.

2. **[mail_triage.py:175](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L175) & [telegram_bot.py:475](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/agents/telegram_bot.py#L475) — Low (Bug): `/mail` increments `listed` during the shadow week (and every time Sheep runs `/mail`), which will prematurely expire carry-over items when `BRIEFING` is turned on or when `/mail` is viewed multiple times.**
   - `send_mail()` calls `mail_triage.mark(conn, ids)`, which increments `listed = listed + 1` for every item returned by `mail_text()` (up to 20 items, including `reply` and `act`).
   - Meanwhile, `briefing_items()` ([mail_triage.py:145-L147](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L145-L147)) filters `reply` items by `t.listed <= CARRY` (2), `act` items without a due date by `t.listed = 0`, `action IS NULL` by `t.listed = 0`, and `fyi`/`ignore` by `t.listed = 0`.
   - Once `BRIEFING = True`, if Sheep checks `/mail` at 08:00 (before the 10:00 timer or before calling `"Leo"`), `/mail` increments `listed` from `0` to `1`. Then at 10:00, `briefing_items()` will **drop** all `act (due IS NULL)`, `Unsorted (action IS NULL)`, and `fyi`/`ignore` counts from the morning briefing because `t.listed` is already `1`! And if Sheep runs `/mail` 3 times in a morning, even `reply` items (`t.listed <= 2`) disappear from the morning briefing before the briefing is ever sent!
   - **Fix:** Either don't call `mail_triage.mark(conn, ids)` in `send_mail()` (so `listed` strictly tracks *briefing* deliveries, while `/mail` always shows `t.day >= _since(today, WINDOW_DAYS)`), or only call `mark()` in `send_mail()` when `not mail_triage.BRIEFING` and `listed == 0`. Not calling `mark()` in `send_mail()` at all is simplest: `/mail` queries by `t.day >= _since(today, WINDOW_DAYS)` and doesn't use `listed` anyway!

3. **[mail_triage.py:100](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L100) vs [mail_triage.py:176](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L176) — Low (Accuracy): `mail_text()` checks `waiting = len(candidates(conn, today))` without calling `mail.index(conn)` first.**
   - `mail-sync.service` runs `mail_index_agent.py` on `live` every 30 minutes, so `live` is indexed, but on `candidate` or `scratch` (or if `fill_headers` hasn't run on newly synced mail, since `mail_index_agent.py` does run `mail.index(conn)` which now populates `from_me`/`bulk`), `mail_text()` works on `live` as long as `mail_index_agent.py` uses the new `mail.index()`. Confirmed `mail.index()` populates `facts(msg, me)`, so `live` is fine; no change required unless `/mail` is tested on candidate without running `mail_index_agent`.

4. **[telegram_bot.py:1107-L1108](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/agents/telegram_bot.py#L1107-L1108) — Low (Edge case): Replying to a `leo_mail` message with a bare `👍` or `👎` emoji.**
   - In `_message()`, `if emojis:` (line 1107) comes *before* the `sent_by(...) == mail_triage.AGENT` intercept (line 1111).
   - An un-replied bare `👍` rightly skips `leo_mail` via `feedback.last_agent_message()` (tested at [test_mail_triage.py:197](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/tests/test_mail_triage.py#L197)).
   - However, if Sheep explicitly *replies* to the `leo_mail` briefing message with a bare `👍` or `👎` text message (`to_bot` is True, `replied.get("message_id")` is the `leo_mail` message id), `emoji_feedback()` records a reaction on the `leo_mail` message in `agent_feedback` and says `"Noted 👍"`, instead of telling Sheep to use `/mail`'s per-item buttons (and without setting `mail_triage.verdict`). No privacy leak (since `leo_mail` is not in `CLOUD_SENDERS` and `agent_feedback` is in `LOCAL_TABLES`), so this is minor.

---

### Verdict

**CHANGES NEEDED** (for Findings #1 and #2):
1. In [mail_triage.py:89](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/shared/mail_triage.py#L89), validate `due` with `date.fromisoformat()` inside `sort_one()` so an invalid date like `"2026-02-29"` or `"2026-11-31"` becomes `None` instead of crashing `_line()`. Add a test case to `test_sort_one_validates_the_answer`.
2. In [telegram_bot.py:475-L476](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system-candidate/agents/telegram_bot.py#L475-L476), remove `mail_triage.mark(conn, ids)` from `send_mail()` so checking `/mail` doesn't increment `listed` and cause `act`/`Unsorted`/`fyi`/`reply` items to vanish from the morning briefing. Add a test verifying that running `/mail` before `leo.deliver()` does not suppress items from `briefing_text()`.
